name: Rohrberg
kurzbeschreibung: Charming, rustic village in the Zillertal with authentic scenery, historic farmhouses, and breathtaking mountain views.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Rohrberg is situated in the Zillertal valley within the Schwaz district, scattered across the sunny southwestern mountain slopes above Zell am Ziller, home to around 580 residents. The municipality extends from the valley floor along the Ziller River at 675 metres across lush meadows and traditional hillside farmsteads up to the ridge of the Kitzbühel Alps, crowned by the Kreuzjoch peak (2,558 m) and the Karspitze (2,195 m). Rohrberg preserves its alpine farming heritage with scattered hamlets and historic timber homesteads. Concurrently, the village forms the central access hub for the world-famous Zillertal Arena, hosting both the valley and middle stations of the Rosenalmbahn gondola.

Geschichte

Rohrberg was first documented in 1350. Alongside Zell am Ziller and Hainzenberg, it belongs to the historic gold-mining communities of the valley, where active gold mining operated from the 16th century until 1838. In the valley hamlet of Rohr, an ore-stamping mill once processed the precious gold-bearing rock. The administration was headquartered in the Gallerhaus mansion, later renowned as Villa Kraus. Granted in 1974, the municipal coat of arms displays three reeds on a golden three-peaked mount, symbolizing both the village name and the gold-mining heritage. Rohrberg became an independent municipality in 1817, maintaining close cultural bonds with neighbouring Zell am Ziller.

Anreise

Reaching Rohrberg is straightforward. Motorists leave the Inntalautobahn A12 at exit Wiesing/Zillertal and follow the B169 Zillertalstraße for about 25 kilometres to Zell am Ziller. The valley terminal of the Rosenalmbahn gondola is located conveniently on the valley floor in Rohrberg territory. The scenic L218 mountain road winds up to the hillside hamlets. Rail passengers travel via ÖBB to Jenbach and switch to the narrow-gauge Zillertalbahn to Zell am Ziller station, where free ski shuttles connect to the gondola in just three minutes.

Tipps

A premier family attraction during summer is the 5,000-square-metre Spruce Tree Castle (Fichtenschloss) on the Rosenalm (1,744 m), featuring four 18-metre wooden towers, marble runs, treetop walkways, and water adventure areas. Just a short stroll away lies Lake Fichtensee, offering boat rentals, swimming pontoons, and sun loungers set against the Zillertal Alps. Hikers can visit the Grindlalm pasture and ascend to the Kreuzjoch summit (2,558 m). In winter, the Rosenalmbahn provides seamless access to the Zillertal Arena ski network, featuring 150 kilometres of groomed slopes extending across Gerlos to Königsleiten.
